episode.title: Publish session forks and torn-tail repairs atomically
episode.before: At parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2, torn-tail recovery rewrote the live session file directly with its valid prefix. Forking created the destination header first and then appended copied entries, lane pointers, the session name, and labels one mutation at a time. A failure during either operation could therefore expose a damaged existing session or a discoverable partial fork.
episode.after: At a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0, the filesystem abstraction supports atomic rename-and-replace. Forks and torn-tail repairs construct a complete sibling temporary file and publish it with one rename; failures remove the temporary file while leaving the destination absent or unchanged. Fork snapshot mutations are generated centrally from session state and reused by memory and JSONL storage.
episode.diff: Added a rename operation to the execution environment; added a stage-then-rename publication helper; routed torn-tail repair and JSONL fork creation through atomic publication; moved fork selection and mutation sequencing into the session-state owner; reduced the repository layer to path/header preparation and storage delegation; added failure-injection tests for staging, rename, repair, append-queue recovery, and replay validation.

evidence_units.claim: Commit a838c069e6318edee8317eff759b74c3934745f0 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 7707 and has parent fadb74f684aaa7755463593e0564b58f9ed081e2.
The parent implementation repaired a torn final JSONL mutation by writing the valid prefix directly to the live session path.

The parent fork implementation created the destination session before copying entries, lanes, name, and labels through separate awaited appends, allowing intermediate destination states to become visible.
The new publication helper populates a deterministic sibling .tmp file, atomically renames it over the destination, and removes the temporary file on population or rename failure.
Torn-tail recovery now stages the valid prefix and publishes it through the atomic replacement helper instead of rewriting the live file directly.
Fork creation builds a temporary target containing the header and all selected mutations, publishes it atomically, and reloads the committed destination.
Session state now computes the complete ordered fork mutation sequence for tree or branch scope, including lane pointers, name, and labels, with fresh consecutive sequence numbers.
The repository prepares the destination identity and delegates fork publication to the source storage, while ordinary creation delegates file initialization to storage.
The execution environment implements rename-and-replace and reports a failed rename against the source path.
Filesystem tests verify that rename removes the source, replaces an existing destination, preserves the destination when the source is missing, and reports the missing source path.
Failure-injection tests verify that failed fork staging or failed atomic rename publishes no fork and leaves no temporary file.
A failure-injection test verifies that interrupted torn-tail staging preserves the original session bytes and removes the temporary file.
Fork conformance assertions verify that a reopened fork retains selected entries, lanes, name, and labels and excludes operation records.
An append failure test verifies that failed durable append does not advance in-memory state or poison the serialized write queue; the next append commits with sequence one and survives reopening.

The change modifies ten agent implementation and test files, adding 407 lines and removing 126 lines, with commit messages explicitly describing crash-safe JSONL publication and relocation of file creation, forking, and fork mutation construction.

candidate_atomics.name: provide-atomic-file-replacement
candidate_atomics.description: Expose a filesystem operation that replaces a destination by renaming a fully prepared source file and preserves actionable source-path errors.

semantic_action.intent: Provide the commit primitive required to publish complete durable state in one visible transition.
semantic_action.pre_state: A complete staged file exists beside a destination that may be absent or contain an older valid state.
semantic_action.post_state: A successful operation removes the staged source and makes its complete contents the destination; a missing source does not alter an existing destination.
semantic_action.validation: Exercise replacement of an existing destination and a missing-source failure, asserting source removal, destination contents, destination preservation, and error path.

candidate_atomics.name: publish-complete-state-atomically
candidate_atomics.description: Populate a sibling temporary file, rename it over the destination only after completion, and clean up staging artifacts on failure.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent interrupted multi-write construction or repair from exposing partial durable state.
semantic_action.pre_state: Publishing the target requires one or more writes, and the destination must remain absent or retain its previous valid contents until all writes succeed.
semantic_action.post_state: The destination changes only through one atomic rename after complete staging; population or rename failure leaves no published partial state and performs best-effort temporary-file cleanup.
semantic_action.validation: Inject failures during staging and rename, then assert the new object is not listed or the existing object remains byte-for-byte unchanged, and no .tmp file remains.

candidate_atomics.name: derive-canonical-fork-mutations
candidate_atomics.description: Generate one ordered, validated mutation sequence representing the selected branch or tree plus its lanes and retained metadata.

semantic_action.intent: Represent a fork as a complete storage-neutral snapshot before durable publication.
semantic_action.pre_state: A source session has entries, lane pointers, and optional name and labels, and fork scope and position select the state to retain.
semantic_action.post_state: A deterministic sequence beginning at one contains the selected entries, resulting lane pointers, name, and applicable labels, while invalid non-message fork targets are rejected.
semantic_action.validation: Reopen a persisted fork and compare retained entries, lanes, name, labels, and excluded records with the selected source state.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-write-continuity-after-append-failure
candidate_atomics.description: Apply in-memory mutations only after durable append succeeds and keep the serialization queue usable after a rejected write.

semantic_action.intent: Keep volatile session state and subsequent writes consistent with durable state after an append failure.
semantic_action.pre_state: A queued mutation's durable append may fail before the mutation is applied to in-memory state.
semantic_action.post_state: The failed mutation is absent from memory and disk, the next mutation receives the unconsumed sequence number, and later writes remain executable.
semantic_action.validation: Fail the first append, assert an empty in-memory log, append again, assert sequence one, reopen storage, and assert only the successful mutation exists.

candidate_workflows.name: make-multi-write-session-publication-crash-safe
candidate_workflows.description: Convert fork creation and destructive tail repair from incremental destination mutation into complete staging followed by one atomic publication, while preserving logical fork semantics and post-failure write continuity.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure session creation, forking, repair, and subsequent appends never expose or continue from partially published durable state.
workflow_graph.entry_state: A session operation builds or repairs a durable JSONL object through multiple writes, so interruption can expose a partial fork or damage the prior valid session.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Logical state is derived before publication, complete bytes are staged, the destination transitions atomically, failures preserve the prior visibility boundary and clean staging artifacts, and later queued writes remain consistent.
unresolved_or_deferred: The deterministic temporary filename requires callers to serialize concurrent publications to the same destination; this commit documents that constraint but does not add cross-process locking.
The unchanged unterminated-but-otherwise-valid final-line repair still appends a newline directly rather than using atomic replacement.
No GitHub PR body, review discussion, or status-check results were available in the evidence bundle.

unresolved_questions: The repository tests were inspected but not executed during extraction, so validation claims describe committed test oracles rather than a fresh local run.

The append-queue recovery behavior is directly tested by this change, but the relevant queue implementation was not materially changed in the pinned diff; it is retained as a validated continuity action rather than claimed as newly implemented logic.
